title: Bookmark Shot: save the lines you love from any book
description: Snap a page and swipe a finger over a sentence you love. Only that sentence is saved as text, with the book and page number. Every feature is free.

demo.title: Try a swipe
demo.lead: Rub a finger or your mouse over any sentence on the page below. Only the words you cross land on the card.
demo.author: Henry David Thoreau
demo.text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life, and see if I could not learn what it had to teach, and not, when I came to die, discover that I had not lived. I did not wish to live what was not life, living is so dear; nor did I wish to practise resignation, unless it was quite necessary.
demo.empty: Swipe over a sentence and it shows up here.
demo.note: The web demo uses a ready-made page. The app reads the text from a photo you take. On a keyboard, Tab to a phrase and press Enter to add or remove it.

problem.title: Where do the good lines end up?
problem.text: It's a library book, so you can't mark it. A photo of the page sinks into a camera roll of thousands. Type it into a notes app and the title and page number rarely make it along. Bookmark Shot keeps the sentence, the book and the page with two gestures: snap, then swipe.

features.title: Crooked photo, straight page
features.text:
After you snap a page, line up the four corners and even a slanted shot is flattened like paper. Sharper letters mean better recognition.
Photos already in your library work too.

features.title: Every quote in one place
features.text:
Your books sit in a library of covers and your quotes gather in one list. Search by sentence, note or book title, and heart the ones you want to read again.
Add a book with one cover shot. The title and author are read for you, and the ISBN too if the back-cover barcode is in view.

features.title: Meet the lines you forgot
features.text:
Today's Quote brings back one of your saved quotes every day, along with the note you left. Keep it on your Home Screen or Lock Screen with a widget.
Love it? Turn it into a paper-style card image and share it.

items.q: Are my photos or quotes sent anywhere?
items.a: No. Text recognition runs entirely on your device with Apple Vision, and your photos and quotes never go to a server. It works offline too. See the Privacy Policy below for details.

Text recognition is done by iOS on your device. It reads books in Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese, Russian and most Western European languages, and on recent versions of iOS also Thai, Vietnamese, Turkish, Indonesian, Polish, Czech, Dutch and the Nordic languages. Greek can't be recognized yet.

items.q: How do I pick just the sentence I want?
items.a: After you snap the page, rub a finger over the sentence as if using a highlighter, and only those words are selected. Pinch to zoom for precision. There's also an eraser, Clear All and Whole Page.

items.q: The title or author came out wrong.
items.a: Cover recognition guesses from the size of the lettering, so very decorative covers can trip it up. You can fix the title and author before saving the book.
It's read from the numbers along the edge of the photo. Just correct it in the page field before saving.

items.q: Can I see my quotes on more than one device?
items.a: Yes. If you're signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account and iCloud Drive is on, your books and quotes sync automatically.

items.q: How do I add the widget?
items.a: Touch and hold the Home Screen, tap Edit > Add Widget, and choose Bookmark Shot. For the Lock Screen, touch and hold it, then tap Customize. Today's Quote shows up there.
Check Settings > Bookmark Shot and make sure camera and photo access are allowed. Taking photos needs a real iPhone.
An iPhone with iOS 17.0 or later.

items.q: How do I get in touch?
items.a: Send feedback from the app's Settings (gear) screen or email us at the address below. We usually reply within two or three days.
